source.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה הָיָ֤ה מוֹשֵׁל֙ בְּכָל־הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת מִן־הַנָּהָר֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים מִנְחָ֛ה וְעֹבְדִ֥ים אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River [to the] land of [the] Philistines and to [the] border of Egypt; [they were] bringing tribute and serving Solomon all [the] days of his life.

en.L: And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River [to] the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt. They were bringing tribute and serving Solomon all the days of his life.
en.B: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon throughout his life.
en.R: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and all the way to the border of Egypt. These kingdoms paid him tribute and were under his rule as long as he lived.

es.L: Y Salomón gobernaba sobre todos los reinos desde el Río [hasta] la tierra de los filisteos y hasta la frontera de Egipto. Traían tributo y servían a Salomón todos los días de su vida.
es.B: Salomón gobernaba sobre todos los reinos desde el río Éufrates hasta la tierra de los filisteos y hasta la frontera de Egipto. Le llevaban tributo y le estuvieron sometidos durante toda su vida.
es.R: Salomón gobernaba sobre todos los reinos desde el río Éufrates hasta la tierra de los filisteos y hasta la frontera de Egipto. Esos reinos le pagaban tributo y estuvieron bajo su gobierno mientras él vivió.

fr.L: Et Salomon dominait sur tous les royaumes depuis le Fleuve [jusqu’au] pays des Philistins et jusqu’à la frontière de l’Égypte. Ils apportaient un tribut et servaient Salomon tous les jours de sa vie.
fr.B: Salomon dominait sur tous les royaumes, depuis l’Euphrate jusqu’au pays des Philistins et jusqu’à la frontière de l’Égypte. Ils lui apportaient un tribut et furent soumis à Salomon toute sa vie.
fr.R: Salomon régnait sur tous les royaumes depuis le fleuve Euphrate jusqu’au pays des Philistins, et jusqu’à la frontière de l’Égypte. Ces royaumes lui ont payé un tribut et sont restés sous son autorité tant qu’il a vécu.

sw.L: Sulemani alikuwa akitawala juu ya falme zote tangu Mto [mpaka] nchi ya Wafilisti na mpaka mpaka wa Misri. Walikuwa wakileta kodi na kumtumikia Sulemani siku zote za maisha yake.
sw.B: Sulemani alitawala falme zote tangu Mto Frati mpaka nchi ya Wafilisti, hata mpakani mwa Misri. Falme hizo zililipa kodi na kumtumikia Sulemani maisha yake yote.
sw.R: Sulemani alitawala falme zote tangu Mto Frati mpaka nchi ya Wafilisti, hata kufika mpakani mwa Misri. Falme hizo zilimlipa kodi na zilikuwa chini ya utawala wake muda wote alioishi.

vi.L: Sa-lô-môn cai trị tất cả các vương quốc từ Sông [đến] xứ Phi-li-tin và cho đến biên giới Ai Cập. Họ dâng triều cống và phục dịch Sa-lô-môn suốt những ngày đời vua.
vi.B: Sa-lô-môn cai trị tất cả các vương quốc từ sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến xứ Phi-li-tin và cho đến biên giới Ai Cập. Các nước ấy nộp triều cống và phục dịch Sa-lô-môn suốt đời vua.
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn cai trị tất cả các vương quốc từ sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến xứ Phi-li-tin và cho đến tận biên giới Ai Cập. Các nước ấy nộp cống cho vua và chịu sự cai trị của vua suốt đời vua.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬은 강에서부터 블레셋 사람들의 땅과 이집트 국경에 이르기까지 모든 나라를 다스리고 있었다. 그들은 솔로몬이 사는 모든 날 동안 조공을 바치며 솔로몬을 섬겼다.
ko.B: 솔로몬은 유프라테스 강에서부터 블레셋 사람들의 땅과 이집트 국경에 이르기까지 모든 나라를 다스렸다. 그 나라들은 솔로몬이 사는 동안 조공을 바치며 그를 섬겼다.
ko.R: 솔로몬은 유프라테스 강에서부터 블레셋 사람들의 땅을 지나 이집트 국경에 이르기까지 모든 나라를 다스렸다. 이 나라들은 솔로몬이 살아 있는 동안 그에게 조공을 바치며 그의 다스림을 받았다.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 5 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 4 ends at verse 20, and the account of Solomon's rule, his court and his wisdom (5:1-14 here) is the start of chapter 5. Many Bibles number these verses 4:21-34, and so number the rest of this chapter (5:15-32 here) 5:1-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with the article names the great river of the north-east, the Euphrates, as in the promise of the land to Abraham and to Israel (Genesis 15:18; Deuteronomy 1:7; Joshua 1:4). Solomon's rule reached the borders that promise named.

decisions.choice: from the River to the land of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs "from the River the land of the Philistines" with no word for "to". The sense is the span from the Euphrates to the Philistine coast; 2 Chronicles 9:26, which tells the same thing, has "to".

decisions.choice: bringing tribute and serving: subject kingdoms paying what they owed
decisions.reason: The word here translated "tribute" is the one used for a grain offering, but its first sense is a gift brought to a superior; between kingdoms it is the payment a subject king brings to his overlord (Judges 3:15; 2 Samuel 8:2, 6). "Serving" means being subject to him.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river so that readers know which one "the River" means (m2).

decisions.choice: paid him tribute and were under his rule as long as he lived
decisions.reason: Readable says what "serving" meant for a kingdom (m4) and turns "all the days of his life" into everyday words.

decisions.choice: "el río Éufrates" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): "the River" is the Euphrates; Literal keeps "el Río", Balanced and Readable name it.

decisions.choice: le Fleuve (L); l'Euphrate (B); le fleuve Euphrate (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the River" with a capital, the usual name for the Euphrates; Balanced and Readable name it.

decisions.choice: Mto Frati
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Euphrates ("Frati"), the river "the River" means; Literal keeps "Mto" with a capital.

decisions.choice: "Sông" (L); "sông Ơ-phơ-rát" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the River", capitalised as a name; Balanced and Readable name the Euphrates, as the English does, in the form 2 Samuel 8 uses.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י לֶֽחֶם־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כֹּר֙ סֹ֔לֶת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים כֹּ֖ר קָֽמַח׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] food of Solomon for one day thirty cors [of] fine flour and sixty cors [of] meal,

en.L: And Solomon's food for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,
en.B: Solomon's provisions for a single day were {{units:about 180 bushels|thirty cors}} of fine flour and {{units:about 360 bushels|sixty cors}} of meal,
en.R: Every day Solomon's court used {{units:about 180 bushels|thirty cors}} of fine flour and {{units:about 360 bushels|sixty cors}} of ordinary flour.

es.L: Y la comida de Salomón para un día era treinta coros de flor de harina y sesenta coros de harina,
es.B: Las provisiones de Salomón para un solo día eran {{units:unos 6 600 litros|treinta coros}} de flor de harina y {{units:unos 13 200 litros|sesenta coros}} de harina,
es.R: Cada día la corte de Salomón usaba {{units:unos 6 600 litros|treinta coros}} de harina fina y {{units:unos 13 200 litros|sesenta coros}} de harina común.

fr.L: Et la nourriture de Salomon pour un jour était de trente cors de fleur de farine et de soixante cors de farine,
fr.B: Les provisions de Salomon pour une seule journée étaient de {{units:environ 6 600 litres|trente cors}} de fleur de farine et de {{units:environ 13 200 litres|soixante cors}} de farine,
fr.R: Chaque jour, la cour de Salomon utilisait {{units:environ 6 600 litres|trente cors}} de farine fine et {{units:environ 13 200 litres|soixante cors}} de farine ordinaire.

sw.L: Chakula cha Sulemani kwa siku moja kilikuwa kori thelathini za unga laini na kori sitini za unga,
sw.B: Mahitaji ya Sulemani kwa siku moja yalikuwa {{units:kama lita 6,600|kori thelathini}} za unga laini na {{units:kama lita 13,200|kori sitini}} za unga,
sw.R: Kila siku watu wa ikulu ya Sulemani walitumia {{units:kama lita 6,600|kori thelathini}} za unga laini na {{units:kama lita 13,200|kori sitini}} za unga wa kawaida.

vi.L: Lương thực của Sa-lô-môn cho một ngày là ba mươi cô-rơ bột mịn và sáu mươi cô-rơ bột thường,
vi.B: Lương thực của Sa-lô-môn mỗi ngày gồm {{units:khoảng 6.600 lít|ba mươi cô-rơ}} bột mịn và {{units:khoảng 13.200 lít|sáu mươi cô-rơ}} bột thường,
vi.R: Mỗi ngày triều đình Sa-lô-môn dùng hết {{units:khoảng 6.600 lít|ba mươi cô-rơ}} bột mịn và {{units:khoảng 13.200 lít|sáu mươi cô-rơ}} bột thường.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬의 하루 음식은 고운 밀가루 삼십 고르와 [보통] 밀가루 육십 고르,
ko.B: 솔로몬의 하루 식량은 고운 밀가루 {{units:6,600리터쯤|삼십 고르}}와 보통 밀가루 {{units:13,200리터쯤|육십 고르}},
ko.R: 솔로몬의 왕궁에서는 날마다 고운 밀가루 {{units:6,600리터쯤|삼십 고르}}와 보통 밀가루 {{units:13,200리터쯤|육십 고르}}를 썼다.

decisions.choice: cor: the largest dry measure, about 6 bushels
decisions.reason: The cor held the same as a homer, ten ephahs (Ezekiel 45:14), about 6 bushels. Thirty cors is about 180 bushels and sixty about 360 bushels: food for a very large household every day.

decisions.choice: Solomon's food: the provisions for his whole court
decisions.reason: The word is "bread" in its wide sense of food. What follows feeds not Solomon alone but his household, his officials and everyone who ate at his table (verse 7).

decisions.choice: fine flour and meal: the best flour and ordinary flour
decisions.reason: The first word is the finely ground flour used for offerings and for the best bread (Leviticus 2:1); the second is plain ground meal (Judges 6:19; 1 Samuel 1:24).

decisions.choice: Solomon's court used (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the court, not Solomon alone, as the ones fed (m2).

decisions.choice: "coros" (L); {{units:unos 6 600 litros|treinta coros}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The cor is counted at 220 litres, as the Kings terms note sets; Spanish converts to litres where the English converts (to bushels), and Literal keeps the Hebrew measure "coro".

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 6 600 litres|trente cors}}
decisions.reason: French gives the metric value by default, with the cor (220 litres) as the alternative, as the terms note asks; the English default is in US bushels.

decisions.choice: kama lita 6,600 (metric, with kori as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Swahili gives the metric value by default (a cor is about 220 litres), with the original measure as the alternative, where the English converts to US bushels; Literal keeps "kori".

decisions.choice: "khoảng 6.600 lít" (default); "ba mươi cô-rơ" (alternative)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier Vietnamese books, the units setting gives metric by default (cor 220 litres, as the Kings terms note sets), not the English bushels; Literal keeps the cor.

decisions.choice: Metric measures by default, "고르" as the alternative: cor 220 litres
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note and the Korean style guide: metric with 쯤, the original unit in the span; Literal keeps the cors.

source.text: עֲשָׂרָ֨ה בָקָ֜ר בְּרִאִ֗ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים בָּקָ֛ר רְעִ֖י וּמֵ֣אָה צֹ֑אן לְ֠בַד מֵֽאַיָּ֤ל וּצְבִי֙ וְיַחְמ֔וּר וּבַרְבֻּרִ֖ים אֲבוּסִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: ten cattle fat and twenty cattle [of] pasture and a hundred sheep, apart from deer and gazelle and roebuck and fowl fattened.

en.L: ten fat oxen and twenty pasture oxen and a hundred sheep, apart from deer and gazelles and roebucks and fattened fowl.
en.B: ten fattened cattle, twenty cattle from the pasture and a hundred sheep and goats, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks and fattened birds.
en.R: They also needed ten stall-fed cattle, twenty cattle from the pastures, and a hundred sheep and goats. Besides these there were deer, gazelles, roe deer and fattened birds.

es.L: diez bueyes gordos y veinte bueyes de pasto y cien ovejas, además de ciervos y gacelas y corzos y aves engordadas.
es.B: diez reses engordadas, veinte reses de pasto y cien ovejas y cabras, además de ciervos, gacelas, corzos y aves engordadas.
es.R: También se necesitaban diez reses alimentadas en establo, veinte reses de los pastos y cien ovejas y cabras. Además de estos había ciervos, gacelas, corzos y aves engordadas.

fr.L: dix bœufs gras, et vingt bœufs de pâturage, et cent moutons, sans compter les cerfs, et les gazelles, et les chevreuils, et les volailles engraissées.
fr.B: dix bœufs engraissés, vingt bœufs de pâturage et cent moutons et chèvres, sans compter les cerfs, les gazelles, les chevreuils et les volailles engraissées.
fr.R: Il fallait aussi dix bœufs nourris à l’étable, vingt bœufs des pâturages et cent moutons et chèvres. En plus de cela, il y avait des cerfs, des gazelles, des chevreuils et des volailles engraissées.

sw.L: ng'ombe kumi wanono na ng'ombe ishirini wa malishoni na kondoo mia moja, mbali na kulungu na paa na swala na kuku walionona.
sw.B: ng'ombe kumi walionenepeshwa, ng'ombe ishirini wa malishoni na kondoo na mbuzi mia moja, zaidi ya kulungu, paa, swala na ndege walionenepeshwa.
sw.R: Walihitaji pia ng'ombe kumi waliolishwa zizini, ng'ombe ishirini wa malishoni, na kondoo na mbuzi mia moja. Zaidi ya hao kulikuwa na kulungu, paa, swala na ndege walionenepeshwa.

vi.L: mười con bò béo, hai mươi con bò đồng cỏ và một trăm con chiên, ngoài ra còn có nai, linh dương, hoẵng và gia cầm vỗ béo.
vi.B: mười con bò vỗ béo, hai mươi con bò nuôi ngoài đồng cỏ và một trăm con chiên dê, ngoài ra còn có nai, linh dương, hoẵng và gia cầm vỗ béo.
vi.R: Họ cũng cần mười con bò nuôi trong chuồng, hai mươi con bò nuôi ngoài đồng cỏ, và một trăm con chiên dê. Ngoài ra còn có nai, linh dương, hoẵng và gia cầm vỗ béo.

ko.L: 살진 소 열 마리와 목장의 소 스무 마리와 양 백 마리, 그 밖에 사슴과 가젤과 노루와 살진 새들이었다.
ko.B: 우리에서 살찌운 소 열 마리, 목장에서 기른 소 스무 마리, 양과 염소 백 마리였고, 그 밖에도 사슴과 가젤과 노루와 살진 새들이 있었다.
ko.R: 또 우리에서 살찌운 소 열 마리, 목장에서 기른 소 스무 마리, 양과 염소 백 마리가 필요했다. 그 밖에도 사슴과 가젤과 노루와 살진 새들이 있었다.

decisions.choice: fat cattle and pasture cattle: animals fattened in stalls and animals brought from grazing
decisions.reason: The first ten were fattened for the table; the next twenty came straight from the pastures. The contrast shows the two kinds of beef served at court.

decisions.choice: sheep: the flock, sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The word names a flock of small livestock and covers both sheep and goats (Leviticus 1:10).

decisions.choice: fattened fowl: a kind of bird kept and fattened for eating
decisions.reason: The word for the birds is found only here, so the exact kind is not known. It may name geese, hens or some other fowl; the point is that they were fattened for the king's table.

decisions.choice: deer, gazelle and roebuck: wild game that Israel could eat
decisions.reason: These three wild animals are named among the clean animals in Deuteronomy 14:5. The third word probably names a roe deer or fallow deer.

decisions.choice: sheep (Literal); sheep and goats (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the single word; Balanced and Readable say that goats were included (m2).

decisions.choice: "chiên" (L); "chiên dê" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The flock is sheep and goats together (meaning decision); Vietnamese "chiên dê" names both, as the English Balanced does.

source.text: כִּי־ה֞וּא רֹדֶ֣ה׀בְּכָל־עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֗ר מִתִּפְסַח֙ וְעַד־עַזָּ֔ה בְּכָל־מַלְכֵ֖י עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשָׁל֗וֹם הָ֥יָה ל֛וֹ מִכָּל־עֲבָרָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: For he [was] ruling over all [the region] beyond the River, from Tiphsah and to Gaza, over all [the] kings beyond the River; and peace was to him from all his sides round about.

en.L: For he was ruling over all [the region] beyond the River, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; and he had peace on all his sides around [him].
en.B: For he had dominion over the whole region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the Euphrates, and he had peace on every side all around him.
en.R: This was because he ruled over all the land west of the Euphrates River, from the town of Tiphsah all the way to Gaza. All the kings of that region were under him, and he was at peace with all the nations around him.

es.L: Porque él dominaba sobre toda [la región] al otro lado del Río, desde Tifsa hasta Gaza, sobre todos los reyes al otro lado del Río; y tenía paz por todos sus lados alrededor.
es.B: Porque él dominaba sobre toda la región al oeste del Éufrates, desde Tifsa hasta Gaza, sobre todos los reyes al oeste del Éufrates, y tenía paz por todos lados a su alrededor.
es.R: Esto se debía a que gobernaba sobre toda la tierra al oeste del río Éufrates, desde el pueblo de Tifsa hasta Gaza. Todos los reyes de esa región estaban bajo su mando, y él estaba en paz con todas las naciones que lo rodeaban.

fr.L: Car il dominait sur toute [la région] au-delà du Fleuve, depuis Tiphsah jusqu’à Gaza, sur tous les rois au-delà du Fleuve ; et il avait la paix de tous ses côtés, alentour.
fr.B: Car il avait autorité sur toute la région à l’ouest de l’Euphrate, depuis Tiphsah jusqu’à Gaza, sur tous les rois à l’ouest de l’Euphrate, et il avait la paix de tous côtés autour de lui.
fr.R: C’est parce qu’il régnait sur tout le pays à l’ouest du fleuve Euphrate, depuis la ville de Tiphsah jusqu’à Gaza. Tous les rois de cette région lui étaient soumis, et il était en paix avec toutes les nations autour de lui.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeye alikuwa akitawala juu ya [eneo] lote ng'ambo ya Mto, tangu Tifsa mpaka Gaza, juu ya wafalme wote wa ng'ambo ya Mto; naye alikuwa na amani pande zake zote kumzunguka.
sw.B: Kwa maana alitawala eneo lote la magharibi ya Frati, tangu Tifsa mpaka Gaza, juu ya wafalme wote wa magharibi ya Frati, naye alikuwa na amani pande zote kumzunguka.
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa kwa sababu alitawala nchi yote iliyo magharibi ya Mto Frati, tangu mji wa Tifsa mpaka Gaza. Wafalme wote wa eneo hilo walikuwa chini yake, naye alikuwa na amani na mataifa yote yaliyomzunguka.

vi.L: Vì vua cai trị toàn [miền] bên kia Sông, từ Típ-sắc đến Ga-xa, trên tất cả các vua bên kia Sông; và vua được bình an về mọi phía chung quanh.
vi.B: Vì vua cai trị cả vùng phía tây sông Ơ-phơ-rát, từ Típ-sắc đến Ga-xa, trên tất cả các vua phía tây sông Ơ-phơ-rát, và vua được thái bình mọi phía chung quanh.
vi.R: Đó là vì vua cai trị cả vùng phía tây sông Ơ-phơ-rát, từ thành Típ-sắc cho đến Ga-xa. Tất cả các vua trong vùng ấy đều phục vua, và vua sống hòa bình với tất cả các nước chung quanh.

ko.L: 그가 강 건너편 모든 [지역], 곧 딥사에서 가사까지, 강 건너편의 모든 왕을 다스리고 있었기 때문이다. 그리고 그에게는 사방 둘레에 평화가 있었다.
ko.B: 그가 유프라테스 강 서쪽 지역 전체, 곧 딥사에서 가사까지 유프라테스 강 서쪽의 모든 왕을 다스렸기 때문이다. 그리고 그의 사방에는 평화가 있었다.
ko.R: 솔로몬은 유프라테스 강 서쪽의 모든 땅, 곧 딥사 성읍에서 가사까지 다스렸기 때문이다. 그 지역의 모든 왕이 그의 다스림을 받았다. 그리고 그는 주변의 모든 나라와 평화롭게 지냈다.

decisions.choice: beyond the River: the lands west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The phrase looks at the land from the far side of the Euphrates, as the great empires to the east did; later it became the name of the province west of the river (Ezra 4:10-11). Here it means all the land from the Euphrates to the Mediterranean.

decisions.choice: Tiphsah and Gaza: the far north-east and the far south-west
decisions.reason: Tiphsah was a crossing place on the Euphrates; Gaza was the southernmost of the Philistine cities on the coast. Between them lies the whole region verse 1 describes.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the great supplies
decisions.reason: The verse explains verses 2-3: such a court could be fed because so many lands were under Solomon's rule.

decisions.choice: peace on every side: the rest Yahweh had promised
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:10 promised rest from enemies all around, and 2 Samuel 7:1, 11 speaks of it under David. Solomon will point to this peace as the sign that the time has come to build the house (5:18).

decisions.choice: beyond the River (Literal); west of the Euphrates (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which side of the river is meant, from the reader's point of view (m1).

decisions.choice: the town of Tiphsah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tiphsah is a town, since few readers will know the name.

source.text: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ יְהוּדָ֨ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לָבֶ֗טַח אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֤חַת גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt Judah and Israel in security, each under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan and to Beersheba, all [the] days of Solomon.

en.L: And Judah and Israel dwelt in security, each under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
en.B: Judah and Israel lived in safety, {{gender:everyone|every man}} under {{gender:their|his}} own vine and under {{gender:their|his}} own fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all through Solomon's lifetime.
en.R: As long as Solomon lived, the people of Judah and Israel were safe, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south. Every family could sit in peace under its own grapevine and its own fig tree.

es.L: Y Judá e Israel habitaban seguros, cada uno debajo de su vid y debajo de su higuera, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, todos los días de Salomón.
es.B: Judá e Israel vivían seguros, cada uno debajo de su propia vid y de su propia higuera, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, durante toda la vida de Salomón.
es.R: Mientras Salomón vivió, la gente de Judá y de Israel estuvo segura, desde Dan en el extremo norte hasta Beerseba en el extremo sur. Cada familia podía sentarse en paz debajo de su propia parra y de su propia higuera.

fr.L: Et Juda et Israël habitèrent en sécurité, chacun sous sa vigne et sous son figuier, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, tous les jours de Salomon.
fr.B: Juda et Israël vécurent en sécurité, chacun sous sa vigne et sous son figuier, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, pendant toute la vie de Salomon.
fr.R: Tant que Salomon a vécu, les gens de Juda et d’Israël ont été en sécurité, depuis Dan, tout au nord, jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, tout au sud. Chaque famille pouvait s’asseoir en paix sous sa vigne et sous son figuier.

sw.L: Yuda na Israeli wakakaa salama, kila mtu chini ya mzabibu wake na chini ya mtini wake, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, siku zote za Sulemani.
sw.B: Watu wa Yuda na Israeli waliishi salama, kila mtu chini ya mzabibu wake na chini ya mtini wake, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, maisha yote ya Sulemani.
sw.R: Muda wote Sulemani alipoishi, watu wa Yuda na Israeli walikuwa salama, tangu Dani upande wa kaskazini kabisa mpaka Beer-sheba upande wa kusini kabisa. Kila jamaa ingeweza kuketi kwa amani chini ya mzabibu wake na mtini wake.

vi.L: Giu-đa và Y-sơ-ra-ên sống an ổn, ai nấy dưới cây nho mình và dưới cây vả mình, từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, suốt những ngày của Sa-lô-môn.
vi.B: Suốt đời Sa-lô-môn, Giu-đa và Y-sơ-ra-ên sống an ổn, mọi người ngồi dưới cây nho và cây vả của mình, từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba.
vi.R: Suốt đời Sa-lô-môn, dân Giu-đa và Y-sơ-ra-ên được bình yên, từ Đan ở tận phía bắc đến Bê-e-Sê-ba ở tận phía nam. Mỗi gia đình đều có thể ngồi yên ổn dưới cây nho và cây vả của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬의 모든 날 동안 단에서 브엘세바까지 유다와 이스라엘이 각자 자기 포도나무 아래와 자기 무화과나무 아래에서 안전하게 살았다.
ko.B: 솔로몬이 사는 동안 단에서 브엘세바까지 유다와 이스라엘 사람들은 저마다 자기 포도나무와 자기 무화과나무 아래에서 평안히 살았다.
ko.R: 솔로몬이 살아 있는 동안, 북쪽 끝 단에서 남쪽 끝 브엘세바까지 유다와 이스라엘 백성은 안전하게 살았다. 집집마다 자기 포도나무와 무화과나무 아래에서 평안히 쉴 수 있었다.

decisions.choice: each under his vine and under his fig tree: living in peace and plenty on one's own land
decisions.reason: To sit under one's own vine and fig tree is a picture of a settled life without fear, eating the fruit of one's own land (Micah 4:4; Zechariah 3:10; 2 Kings 18:31).

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land, north to south
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba the southernmost; the pair stands for the whole country (Judges 20:1; 1 Samuel 3:20).

decisions.choice: each: every household, men and women alike
decisions.reason: The word means "each man", but it is used for every person in the land; the whole people lived in safety, not the men only.

decisions.choice: everyone ... their own (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the gender setting, since the whole people is meant (m3); Literal keeps the single Hebrew word as "each".

decisions.choice: every family could sit in peace; in the far north ... in the far south (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains both pictures (m1, m2): who lived under the vines, and where Dan and Beersheba lay.

decisions.choice: "cada uno ... su propia vid", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Balanced offers "everyone ... their" against "every man ... his" (r-en-1). Spanish "cada uno" with "su" already reads as every person, man or woman, so there is no second Spanish wording to put in a span.

decisions.choice: chacun sous sa vigne
decisions.reason: French "chacun" already means anyone, man or woman, so Balanced needs no gender span where the English has one, as the French style guide says of generic pronouns.

decisions.choice: kila mtu (no gender span)
decisions.reason: "Kila mtu" (every person) already includes men and women, so Swahili has no second wording for the English gender setting here.

decisions.choice: "mọi người ... của mình" with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender span "mọi người" / "mỗi người đàn ông"
decisions.reason: Every household, men and women alike (meaning decision); Vietnamese "mọi người" and "của mình" already include both, so the English gender setting has no counterpart, as in the Vietnamese Samuel.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "저마다" already covers men and women
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: As the Samuel note: Korean words for people are already inclusive, so the English Balanced span has nothing to change in Korean.

decisions.choice: "단에서 브엘세바까지"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note; Readable adds north and south as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אֻרְוֺ֥ת סוּסִ֖ים לְמֶרְכָּב֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were to Solomon forty thousand stalls [of] horses for his chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.

en.L: And Solomon had 40,000 stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.
en.B: Solomon had 40,000 stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.
en.R: Solomon had 40,000 stalls for the horses that pulled his chariots, and he had 12,000 horsemen.

es.L: Y tenía Salomón 40 000 establos de caballos para sus carros, y 12 000 jinetes.
es.B: Salomón tenía 40 000 establos de caballos para sus carros, y 12 000 jinetes.
es.R: Salomón tenía 40 000 establos para los caballos que tiraban de sus carros, y tenía 12 000 jinetes.

fr.L: Et Salomon avait 40 000 stalles de chevaux pour ses chars, et 12 000 cavaliers.
fr.B: Salomon avait 40 000 stalles de chevaux pour ses chars, et 12 000 cavaliers.
fr.R: Salomon avait 40 000 places dans ses écuries pour les chevaux qui tiraient ses chars, et il avait 12 000 cavaliers.

sw.L: Sulemani alikuwa na mabanda elfu arobaini ya farasi kwa ajili ya magari yake ya vita, na wapanda farasi elfu kumi na mbili.
sw.B: Sulemani alikuwa na mabanda elfu arobaini ya farasi kwa ajili ya magari yake ya vita, na wapanda farasi elfu kumi na mbili.
sw.R: Sulemani alikuwa na mabanda elfu arobaini ya farasi waliovuta magari yake ya vita, naye alikuwa na wapanda farasi elfu kumi na mbili.

vi.L: Sa-lô-môn có 40.000 chuồng ngựa cho các xe của vua, và 12.000 kỵ binh.
vi.B: Sa-lô-môn có 40.000 chuồng ngựa cho các xe chiến mã của vua, và 12.000 kỵ binh.
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn có 40.000 chuồng cho những con ngựa kéo xe chiến mã của vua, và vua có 12.000 kỵ binh.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬에게는 그의 병거들을 위한 말 외양간 4만 칸과 기병 1만 2천 명이 있었다.
ko.B: 솔로몬에게는 병거를 끄는 말을 위한 마구간이 4만 칸 있었고, 기병이 1만 2천 명 있었다.
ko.R: 솔로몬에게는 병거를 끄는 말들을 위한 마구간이 4만 칸 있었고, 기병도 1만 2천 명이나 있었다.

decisions.choice: 40,000 stalls, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 9:25, which tells the same thing, has 4,000 stalls, and 1 Kings 10:26 gives Solomon 1,400 chariots, which fits the smaller number better. A copyist may have changed one number; this translation keeps the number the Hebrew text of Kings has.

decisions.choice: horsemen: riders, or possibly chariot horses
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but it can also name the horses themselves; beside the stalls and chariots either sense is possible (10:26).

decisions.choice: many horses: what the law warned a king against
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:16 told Israel's king not to gather many horses for himself. The narrator lists Solomon's horses without comment here, but the reader is meant to remember that law (10:26-29; 11:1-4).

decisions.choice: numbers in words below a hundred thousand ("40 000", "12 000")
decisions.reason: Spanish writes round thousands in words in narrative, as the Spanish of Samuel does; larger counts with several figures are written in digits with a space for thousands, as the Pentateuch note sets.

decisions.choice: numbers in words ("elfu arobaini")
decisions.reason: Swahili writes counts in words in running text, as the style guide asks, where the English uses figures; measures stay in figures. Used through this block.

decisions.choice: numbers above one hundred in figures with a dot (40.000; 12.000)
decisions.reason: As the later Vietnamese Samuel blocks do, large numbers are written in figures, with the Vietnamese thousands point.

source.text: וְכִלְכְּלוּ֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְאֵ֧ת כָּל־הַקָּרֵ֛ב אֶל־שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ חָדְשׁ֑וֹ לֹ֥א יְעַדְּר֖וּ דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And supplied these officers King Solomon and all the [one] approaching to [the] table of King Solomon, each [in] his month; not they let lack a thing.

en.L: And these officers supplied King Solomon and all who came near to the table of King Solomon, each [in] his month; they let nothing be lacking.
en.B: These officers provided for King Solomon and for everyone who came to King Solomon's table, each in his month. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.
en.R: Solomon's twelve district officers each took a month to provide food for King Solomon and for everyone who ate at the king's table. They made sure there was always enough.

es.L: Y estos gobernadores abastecían al rey Salomón y a todos los que se acercaban a la mesa del rey Salomón, cada uno [en] su mes; no dejaban que faltara nada.
es.B: Estos gobernadores abastecían al rey Salomón y a todos los que comían a la mesa del rey Salomón, cada uno en su mes. Se encargaban de que no faltara nada.
es.R: Cada uno de los doce gobernadores de distrito de Salomón tenía un mes para dar la comida al rey Salomón y a todos los que comían a la mesa del rey. Se aseguraban de que siempre hubiera suficiente.

fr.L: Et ces intendants pourvoyaient [aux besoins du] roi Salomon et de tous ceux qui s’approchaient de la table du roi Salomon, chacun [en] son mois ; ils ne laissaient rien manquer.
fr.B: Ces intendants approvisionnaient le roi Salomon et tous ceux qui venaient à la table du roi Salomon, chacun pendant son mois. Ils veillaient à ce que rien ne manque.
fr.R: Les douze gouverneurs de district de Salomon fournissaient à tour de rôle, un mois chacun, la nourriture pour le roi Salomon et pour tous ceux qui mangeaient à la table du roi. Ils faisaient en sorte qu’il y en ait toujours assez.

sw.L: Wasimamizi hao wakampatia mfalme Sulemani mahitaji, na wote waliokaribia meza ya mfalme Sulemani, kila mmoja [katika] mwezi wake; hawakuacha kitu kipungue.
sw.B: Wasimamizi hao walimpatia mfalme Sulemani mahitaji, pamoja na wote waliokuja mezani pa mfalme Sulemani, kila mmoja katika mwezi wake. Walihakikisha kwamba hakuna kilichopungua.
sw.R: Wakuu kumi na wawili wa wilaya za Sulemani walipeana zamu ya mwezi mmoja kila mmoja kuleta chakula cha mfalme Sulemani na cha kila mtu aliyekula mezani pa mfalme. Walihakikisha kwamba chakula kilitosha daima.

vi.L: Các quan cai trị ấy cung cấp cho vua Sa-lô-môn và mọi người đến gần bàn của vua Sa-lô-môn, mỗi người [trong] tháng của mình; họ không để thiếu một thứ gì.
vi.B: Các quan cai trị ấy lo cung cấp cho vua Sa-lô-môn và mọi người được dự bàn ăn của vua Sa-lô-môn, mỗi người trong tháng của mình. Họ lo sao cho không thiếu một thứ gì.
vi.R: Mười hai quan cai trị các vùng của Sa-lô-môn, mỗi người lo một tháng, cung cấp lương thực cho vua Sa-lô-môn và mọi người ăn tại bàn của vua. Họ lo sao cho lúc nào cũng có đủ.

ko.L: 그리고 이 관장들이 솔로몬 왕과 솔로몬 왕의 상에 가까이 오는 모든 사람을 위하여 각자 자기 달에 [식량을] 공급했다. 그들은 부족한 것이 하나도 없게 했다.
ko.B: 이 관장들은 각자 맡은 달에 솔로몬 왕과 왕의 식탁에 함께하는 모든 사람을 위하여 식량을 공급했다. 그들은 부족한 것이 하나도 없게 했다.
ko.R: 솔로몬의 지방 관장 열두 명은 한 달씩 돌아가며 솔로몬 왕과 왕의 식탁에서 먹는 모든 사람에게 음식을 공급했다. 그들은 음식이 언제나 넉넉하도록 신경을 썼다.

decisions.choice: these officers: the twelve district officers of 4:7-19
decisions.reason: Solomon had divided the land into twelve districts, each under an officer who supplied the king's household for one month of the year (4:7). The account of Solomon's rule in verses 1-6 interrupts the list, and this verse returns to it.

decisions.choice: all who came near to the king's table: everyone fed at court
decisions.reason: To come to the king's table means to eat at the king's expense: his family, officials, guests and those he honored (2:7; 2 Samuel 9:7, 13).

decisions.choice: twelve district officers each took a month (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says who "these officers" are and how the months were shared out (m1).

source.text: וְהַשְּׂעֹרִ֣ים וְהַתֶּ֔בֶן לַסּוּסִ֖ים וְלָרָ֑כֶשׁ יָבִ֗אוּ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּמִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the steeds they brought to the place where it was there, each according to his assignment.

en.L: And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the swift steeds they would bring to the place where it should be, each according to his assignment.
en.B: They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift horses to the place where it was needed, each according to his assignment.
en.R: They also brought barley and straw for the horses, including the fast chariot horses. Each officer took his share to the place where it was needed.

es.L: Y la cebada y la paja para los caballos y para los corceles las traían al lugar donde debía estar, cada uno conforme a lo que le estaba asignado.
es.B: También llevaban cebada y paja para los caballos de tiro y para los caballos veloces al lugar donde hacía falta, cada uno según lo que le correspondía.
es.R: También llevaban cebada y paja para los caballos, entre ellos los caballos rápidos de los carros. Cada gobernador llevaba su parte al lugar donde se necesitaba.

fr.L: Et l’orge et la paille pour les chevaux et pour les coursiers, ils les apportaient au lieu où il fallait, chacun selon sa charge.
fr.B: Ils apportaient aussi l’orge et la paille pour les chevaux et les coursiers à l’endroit où on en avait besoin, chacun selon sa charge.
fr.R: Ils apportaient aussi de l’orge et de la paille pour les chevaux, y compris les chevaux rapides des chars. Chaque gouverneur apportait sa part à l’endroit où on en avait besoin.

sw.L: Na shayiri na majani kwa ajili ya farasi na kwa ajili ya farasi wepesi waliileta mahali ilipopaswa kuwa, kila mmoja kwa kadiri ya zamu yake.
sw.B: Pia walileta shayiri na majani kwa ajili ya farasi na farasi wepesi mahali ilipohitajika, kila mmoja kwa kadiri ya zamu yake.
sw.R: Pia walileta shayiri na majani kwa ajili ya farasi, pamoja na farasi wepesi wa magari ya vita. Kila mkuu wa wilaya alipeleka sehemu yake mahali ilipohitajika.

vi.L: Họ cũng đem lúa mạch và rơm cho ngựa và cho ngựa phi nhanh đến nơi cần đến, mỗi người theo phần đã định.
vi.B: Họ cũng đem lúa mạch và rơm cho ngựa kéo xe và ngựa phi nhanh đến nơi cần, mỗi người theo phần được giao.
vi.R: Họ cũng đem lúa mạch và rơm cho ngựa, kể cả những con ngựa kéo xe chạy nhanh. Mỗi quan cai trị đem phần của mình đến nơi cần đến.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 말들과 날랜 말들을 위한 보리와 짚을 각자 맡은 몫대로 그것이 있어야 할 곳으로 가져왔다.
ko.B: 그들은 또 말들과 날랜 말들에게 먹일 보리와 짚을 각자 맡은 대로 필요한 곳으로 가져왔다.
ko.R: 그들은 또 말들에게 먹일 보리와 짚도 가져왔다. 거기에는 병거를 끄는 날랜 말들도 있었다. 관장들은 각자 맡은 몫을 필요한 곳으로 가져갔다.

decisions.choice: steeds: swift horses
decisions.reason: This word names fast horses used for chariots and for royal messengers (Esther 8:10, 14; Micah 1:13).

decisions.choice: the place where it should be: wherever the supplies were needed
alternatives: the place where the king was
the place where the horses were stationed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the place where it would be there" and does not say what "it" is. It may mean wherever the king was, or wherever the horses were kept (9:19; 10:26), or simply the place set for each delivery. The sense is that each officer brought his share to where it was required.

decisions.choice: according to his assignment: the share laid on each officer
decisions.reason: The word often means "judgment" or "custom"; here it is the rule or quota set for each officer.

decisions.choice: fast chariot horses; each officer (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the kind of horse (m1) and says that "each" means each officer.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים חָכְמָ֧ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּתְבוּנָ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְרֹ֣חַב לֵ֔ב כַּח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave God wisdom to Solomon and understanding very much, and breadth of heart like the sand which [is] on [the] shore of the sea.

en.L: And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding very great, and breadth of heart like the sand that [is] on the shore of the sea.
en.B: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and a breadth of mind as vast as the sand on the seashore.
en.R: God made Solomon very wise and gave him great understanding. There was no end to what his mind could take in. It was like the sand on the seashore.

es.L: Y dio Dios a Salomón sabiduría y entendimiento en gran manera, y anchura de corazón como la arena que [está] a la orilla del mar.
es.B: Dios le dio a Salomón sabiduría y un entendimiento muy grande, y una amplitud de mente tan vasta como la arena a la orilla del mar.
es.R: Dios hizo a Salomón muy sabio y le dio gran entendimiento. Su mente no tenía límites para aprender. Era como la arena a la orilla del mar.

fr.L: Et Dieu donna à Salomon de la sagesse et une intelligence extrêmement grande, et une largeur de cœur comme le sable qui [est] sur le bord de la mer.
fr.B: Dieu donna à Salomon la sagesse et une très grande intelligence, et un esprit aussi vaste que le sable du bord de la mer.
fr.R: Dieu a rendu Salomon très sage et lui a donné une grande intelligence. Son esprit pouvait comprendre une quantité infinie de choses, comme le sable au bord de la mer.

sw.L: Mungu akampa Sulemani hekima na ufahamu mwingi sana, na upana wa moyo kama mchanga ulio ufuoni mwa bahari.
sw.B: Mungu alimpa Sulemani hekima na ufahamu mwingi sana, na upana wa akili mkubwa kama mchanga wa ufuoni mwa bahari.
sw.R: Mungu alimfanya Sulemani kuwa na hekima nyingi sana na kumpa ufahamu mkubwa. Akili yake iliweza kufahamu mambo yasiyo na mwisho, kama mchanga wa ufuoni mwa bahari.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời ban cho Sa-lô-môn sự khôn ngoan và sự thông sáng rất lớn, và tấm lòng rộng lớn như cát trên bờ biển.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời ban cho Sa-lô-môn sự khôn ngoan và sự thông sáng rất lớn, với một tâm trí rộng lớn như cát trên bờ biển.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời làm cho Sa-lô-môn rất khôn ngoan và ban cho vua sự hiểu biết lớn lao. Trí óc vua hiểu biết vô cùng, nhiều như cát trên bờ biển.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 솔로몬에게 지혜와 매우 큰 명철과 바닷가의 모래 같은 넓은 마음을 주셨다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 솔로몬에게 지혜와 매우 뛰어난 명철을 주시고, 바닷가의 모래처럼 넓은 마음을 주셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 솔로몬을 매우 지혜롭게 하시고 뛰어난 깨달음을 주셨다. 그의 마음은 바닷가의 모래처럼 넓어서 무엇이든 다 받아들일 수 있었다.

decisions.choice: breadth of heart: a mind of wide range
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and understanding. A broad heart takes in a great many things; the same picture of breadth stands behind verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: like the sand on the seashore: past counting
decisions.reason: The sand of the sea is a picture of what cannot be measured (Genesis 22:17); 4:20 used it for the people of Judah and Israel. Here it is used for Solomon's understanding.

decisions.choice: God gave wisdom: the answer to Solomon's prayer
decisions.reason: This fulfills what God promised at Gibeon: "a wise and discerning heart" (3:9, 12).

decisions.choice: heart (Literal); mind (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mind", since the heart here is the place of understanding (m1).

decisions.choice: "corazón" (L); "mente" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the heart is the seat of thought; Balanced and Readable say "mente".

decisions.choice: "tấm lòng rộng lớn" (L); "tâm trí rộng lớn" (B); "trí óc ... vô cùng" (R)
decisions.reason: A mind of wide range (meaning decision); in Vietnamese "lòng rộng rãi" would mean generosity, so Balanced and Readable name the mind.

decisions.choice: "지혜" and "명철" (L, B), "깨달음" (R); "마음" for *lev*
decisions.reason: As the Psalms and Proverbs note's words for wisdom and understanding; Korean 마음 covers both heart and mind, so no change between levels is needed.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶב֙ חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵֽחָכְמַ֖ת כָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶ֑דֶם וּמִכֹּ֖ל חָכְמַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was great [the] wisdom of Solomon more than [the] wisdom of all [the] sons of [the] east and more than all [the] wisdom of Egypt.

en.L: And the wisdom of Solomon was greater than the wisdom of all the {{gender:people|sons}} of the east and than all the wisdom of Egypt.
en.B: Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the peoples of the east and greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
en.R: Solomon was wiser than all the people of the east and wiser than all the people of Egypt, though they were famous for their wisdom.

es.L: Y la sabiduría de Salomón fue mayor que la sabiduría de todos los hijos del oriente y que toda la sabiduría de Egipto.
es.B: La sabiduría de Salomón era mayor que la de todos los pueblos del oriente y que toda la sabiduría de Egipto.
es.R: Salomón era más sabio que toda la gente del oriente y más sabio que toda la gente de Egipto, aunque ellos eran famosos por su sabiduría.

fr.L: Et la sagesse de Salomon fut plus grande que la sagesse de tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de l’Orient et que toute la sagesse de l’Égypte.
fr.B: La sagesse de Salomon surpassait la sagesse de tous les peuples de l’Orient et toute la sagesse de l’Égypte.
fr.R: Salomon était plus sage que tous les gens de l’Orient et que tous ceux d’Égypte, qui étaient pourtant célèbres pour leur sagesse.

sw.L: Hekima ya Sulemani ikawa kubwa kuliko hekima ya wana wote wa mashariki, na kuliko hekima yote ya Misri.
sw.B: Hekima ya Sulemani ilikuwa kubwa kuliko hekima ya watu wote wa mashariki, na kubwa kuliko hekima yote ya Misri.
sw.R: Sulemani alikuwa na hekima kuliko watu wote wa mashariki, na kuliko watu wote wa Misri, ingawa watu hao walikuwa maarufu kwa hekima yao.

vi.L: Sự khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn lớn hơn sự khôn ngoan của tất cả con cái phương đông và hơn tất cả sự khôn ngoan của Ai Cập.
vi.B: Sự khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn vượt hơn sự khôn ngoan của mọi dân phương đông và mọi sự khôn ngoan của Ai Cập.
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn khôn ngoan hơn tất cả những người phương đông và hơn mọi người Ai Cập, dù họ nổi tiếng là khôn ngoan.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬의 지혜는 동쪽의 모든 자손의 지혜와 이집트의 모든 지혜보다 컸다.
ko.B: 솔로몬의 지혜는 동방의 모든 민족의 지혜보다 뛰어났고, 이집트의 모든 지혜보다도 뛰어났다.
ko.R: 솔로몬은 동방의 모든 사람보다 더 지혜로웠고, 이집트의 모든 사람보다도 더 지혜로웠다. 이 나라들은 지혜로 이름난 곳이었다.

decisions.choice: the people of the east and Egypt: nations famous for wisdom
decisions.reason: The desert peoples to the east (Job 1:3) and Egypt (Genesis 41:8; Isaiah 19:11-12) were known for their wise men and their collections of sayings. Solomon's wisdom outshone the best that was known.

decisions.choice: though they were famous for their wisdom (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds why these nations are named (m1).

decisions.choice: "los hijos del oriente", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "people|sons"; Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so there is no gender span, as the Pentateuch terms list sets for "los hijos de Israel".

decisions.choice: No gender span on "자손"
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: 자손 already means descendants of both sexes, so the English span has nothing to change in Korean.

source.text: וַיֶּחְכַּם֮ מִכָּל־הָֽאָדָם֒ מֵאֵיתָ֣ן הָאֶזְרָחִ֗י וְהֵימָ֧ן וְכַלְכֹּ֛ל וְדַרְדַּ֖ע בְּנֵ֣י מָח֑וֹל וַיְהִֽי־שְׁמ֥וֹ בְכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he was wise more than all the human, more than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman and Calcol and Darda, sons of Mahol; and was his name in all the nations round about.

en.L: And he was wiser than all humankind, than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman and Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his name was in all the nations around.
en.B: He was wiser than anyone else, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His fame spread to all the surrounding nations.
en.R: He was wiser than anyone, even wiser than the famous wise men Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. People in all the nations around Israel heard about him.

es.L: Y fue más sabio que todos los hombres, más que Etán el ezraíta, y Hemán y Calcol y Darda, hijos de Mahol; y su nombre estaba en todas las naciones de alrededor.
es.B: Fue más sabio que cualquier otro, más que Etán el ezraíta, y que Hemán, Calcol y Darda, los hijos de Mahol. Su fama se extendió por todas las naciones vecinas.
es.R: Era más sabio que nadie, más sabio aun que los famosos sabios Etán el ezraíta, Hemán, Calcol y Darda, los hijos de Mahol. La gente de todas las naciones alrededor de Israel oyó hablar de él.

fr.L: Et il fut plus sage que tous les humains, qu’Éthan l’Ezrahite, et Hémân, et Kalkol, et Darda, les fils de Mahol ; et son nom était dans toutes les nations d’alentour.
fr.B: Il était plus sage que quiconque, plus sage qu’Éthan l’Ezrahite, que Hémân, Kalkol et Darda, les fils de Mahol. Sa renommée s’étendit à toutes les nations voisines.
fr.R: Il était plus sage que n’importe qui, plus sage même que des sages célèbres comme Éthan l’Ezrahite, Hémân, Kalkol et Darda, les fils de Mahol. Dans toutes les nations autour d’Israël, on a entendu parler de lui.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa na hekima kuliko wanadamu wote, kuliko Ethani Mwezrahi na Hemani na Kalkoli na Darda, wana wa Maholi; na jina lake likawa katika mataifa yote yaliyozunguka.
sw.B: Alikuwa na hekima kuliko mtu mwingine yeyote, kuliko Ethani Mwezrahi, na Hemani, Kalkoli na Darda, wana wa Maholi. Sifa zake zikaenea katika mataifa yote yaliyozunguka.
sw.R: Alikuwa na hekima kuliko mtu yeyote, hata kuliko wenye hekima maarufu Ethani Mwezrahi, Hemani, Kalkoli na Darda, wana wa Maholi. Watu wa mataifa yote yaliyoizunguka Israeli walisikia habari zake.

vi.L: Vua khôn ngoan hơn mọi người, hơn Ê-than người Ếch-ra, Hê-man, Canh-côn và Đạt-đa, các con trai Ma-hôn; danh tiếng vua [lan] khắp các nước chung quanh.
vi.B: Vua khôn ngoan hơn mọi người, hơn cả Ê-than người Ếch-ra, Hê-man, Canh-côn và Đạt-đa, các con trai Ma-hôn. Danh tiếng vua lan khắp các nước chung quanh.
vi.R: Vua khôn ngoan hơn bất cứ ai, hơn cả những người khôn ngoan nổi tiếng như Ê-than người Ếch-ra, Hê-man, Canh-côn và Đạt-đa, các con trai Ma-hôn. Dân trong mọi nước chung quanh Y-sơ-ra-ên đều nghe nói về vua.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 모든 사람보다, 에스라 사람 에단과 마홀의 아들들인 헤만과 갈골과 다르다보다 더 지혜로웠다. 그리고 그의 이름이 사방 모든 민족 가운데 있었다.
ko.B: 그는 어느 누구보다도 지혜로웠다. 에스라 사람 에단과, 마홀의 아들들인 헤만과 갈골과 다르다보다도 더 지혜로웠다. 그의 명성은 주변의 모든 민족에게 퍼졌다.
ko.R: 그는 어느 누구보다도 지혜로웠다. 이름난 지혜자들인 에스라 사람 에단과, 마홀의 아들들인 헤만과 갈골과 다르다보다도 더 지혜로웠다. 이스라엘 주변의 모든 민족이 그에 대한 소문을 들었다.

decisions.choice: Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Darda: wise men well known in their day
decisions.reason: Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman are named in the titles of Psalms 89 and 88. 1 Chronicles 2:6 lists Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara as sons of Zerah of Judah. Their fame is the measure Solomon's wisdom is set against.

decisions.choice: sons of Mahol: their father's name, or a description
decisions.reason: Mahol may be the name of their father. The word also means "dance", so "sons of Mahol" may describe them as belonging to a guild of musicians or singers, which would fit the psalm titles that name Ethan and Heman.

decisions.choice: his name: his fame
decisions.reason: A person's name stands for his reputation (1 Samuel 18:30).

decisions.choice: the famous wise men (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says why these four are named (m1).

decisions.choice: Éthan l'Ezrahite, Hémân
decisions.reason: The forms of the French Psalm titles (Psalms 88 and 89).

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֕ר שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים מָשָׁ֑ל וַיְהִ֥י שִׁיר֖וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וָאָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and were his songs five and a thousand.

en.L: And he spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs were 1,005.
en.B: He spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs numbered 1,005.
en.R: He spoke 3,000 wise sayings, and he made up 1,005 songs.

es.L: Y pronunció 3000 proverbios, y sus cantares fueron 1005.
es.B: Compuso 3000 proverbios, y sus cantos fueron 1005.
es.R: Dijo 3000 dichos sabios, y compuso 1005 canciones.

fr.L: Et il prononça 3 000 proverbes, et ses chants furent au nombre de 1 005.
fr.B: Il prononça 3 000 proverbes, et ses chants furent au nombre de 1 005.
fr.R: Il a prononcé 3 000 paroles de sagesse, et il a composé 1 005 chants.

sw.L: Akanena mithali elfu tatu, na nyimbo zake zilikuwa elfu moja na tano.
sw.B: Alinena mithali elfu tatu, na nyimbo zake zilikuwa elfu moja na tano.
sw.R: Alisema methali za hekima elfu tatu, akatunga nyimbo elfu moja na tano.

vi.L: Vua nói ra 3.000 câu châm ngôn, và các bài ca của vua [là] 1.005 bài.
vi.B: Vua nói ra 3.000 câu châm ngôn, và sáng tác 1.005 bài ca.
vi.R: Vua nói ra 3.000 câu nói khôn ngoan, và vua sáng tác 1.005 bài hát.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 잠언 3천 개를 말했고, 그의 노래는 1,005편이었다.
ko.B: 그는 잠언을 3천 개나 말했고, 그가 지은 노래는 1,005편이었다.
ko.R: 그는 지혜로운 말을 3천 개나 했고, 노래를 1,005편이나 지었다.

decisions.choice: proverbs: short sayings of wisdom, often comparisons
decisions.reason: The word names a saying that sets one thing beside another to teach a lesson, as in the book of Proverbs (Proverbs 1:1; 10:1; 25:1).

decisions.choice: 1,005 songs, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation gives 5,000 songs. The Hebrew number is kept here.

decisions.choice: his songs: the songs linked with Solomon
decisions.reason: The Song of Songs (1:1) and Psalms 72 and 127 carry Solomon's name in their titles.

decisions.choice: wise sayings; made up (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "proverbs" (m1) and says that the songs were his own.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֮ עַל־הָֽעֵצִים֒ מִן־הָאֶ֨רֶז֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד֙ הָאֵז֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹצֵ֖א בַּקִּ֑יר וַיְדַבֵּר֙ עַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה וְעַל־הָע֔וֹף וְעַל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַל־הַדָּגִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar which [is] in Lebanon and to the hyssop which comes out in the wall; and he spoke about the animals and about the birds and about the creeping things and about the fish.

en.L: And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar that [is] in Lebanon as far as the hyssop that comes out in the wall; and he spoke about the beasts and about the birds and about the creeping things and about the fish.
en.B: He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of the wall, and he spoke about animals, birds, creeping things and fish.
en.R: He spoke about trees and plants, from the great cedars of Lebanon to the little hyssop plant that grows out of cracks in a wall. He also spoke about animals, birds, creatures that crawl on the ground, and fish.

es.L: Y habló de los árboles, desde el cedro que [está] en el Líbano hasta el hisopo que brota en la pared; y habló de los animales y de las aves y de los reptiles y de los peces.
es.B: Habló de los árboles, desde el cedro del Líbano hasta el hisopo que crece en la pared, y habló de los animales, de las aves, de los reptiles y de los peces.
es.R: Habló de árboles y plantas, desde los grandes cedros del Líbano hasta la pequeña planta de hisopo que crece en las grietas de una pared. También habló de animales, aves, animales que se arrastran por el suelo y peces.

fr.L: Et il parla des arbres, depuis le cèdre qui [est] au Liban jusqu’à l’hysope qui sort du mur ; et il parla des bêtes, et des oiseaux, et des reptiles, et des poissons.
fr.B: Il parla des arbres, depuis le cèdre du Liban jusqu’à l’hysope qui pousse sur le mur ; il parla aussi des animaux, des oiseaux, des reptiles et des poissons.
fr.R: Il a parlé des arbres et des plantes, depuis les grands cèdres du Liban jusqu’à la petite plante d’hysope qui pousse dans les fentes des murs. Il a aussi parlé des animaux, des oiseaux, des bêtes qui rampent sur le sol et des poissons.

sw.L: Akanena habari za miti, tangu mwerezi ulio Lebanoni mpaka hisopo itokayo ukutani; akanena habari za wanyama na za ndege na za vitambaavyo na za samaki.
sw.B: Alinena habari za miti, tangu mwerezi wa Lebanoni mpaka hisopo inayoota ukutani; alinena pia habari za wanyama, ndege, viumbe vitambaavyo na samaki.
sw.R: Alizungumza juu ya miti na mimea, tangu mierezi mikubwa ya Lebanoni mpaka mmea mdogo wa hisopo unaoota katika nyufa za ukuta. Alizungumza pia juu ya wanyama, ndege, viumbe vinavyotambaa ardhini, na samaki.

vi.L: Vua nói về cây cối, từ cây bá hương ở Li-ban cho đến cây kinh giới mọc ra từ tường; vua cũng nói về thú vật, chim chóc, loài bò sát và loài cá.
vi.B: Vua nói về cây cối, từ cây bá hương ở Li-ban cho đến cây kinh giới mọc trên tường. Vua cũng nói về thú vật, chim chóc, loài bò sát và loài cá.
vi.R: Vua nói về cây cối, từ những cây bá hương to lớn ở Li-ban cho đến cây kinh giới nhỏ bé mọc ra từ kẽ tường. Vua cũng nói về thú vật, chim chóc, những loài bò trên đất và cá.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 나무들에 대하여, 레바논에 있는 백향목에서부터 벽에서 돋아나는 우슬초까지 말했고, 짐승들과 새들과 기어 다니는 것들과 물고기들에 대하여 말했다.
ko.B: 그는 레바논의 백향목에서부터 담벼락에 자라는 우슬초에 이르기까지 나무에 대하여 말했고, 짐승과 새와 기어 다니는 것과 물고기에 대해서도 말했다.
ko.R: 그는 나무와 풀에 대하여 이야기했다. 레바논의 커다란 백향목에서부터 담벼락 틈에서 자라는 작은 우슬초까지 이야기했다. 또 짐승과 새와 땅에 기어 다니는 것과 물고기에 대해서도 이야기했다.

decisions.choice: spoke about: spoke of, in his sayings and teaching
decisions.reason: The words may mean that he described plants and animals, or that he drew his proverbs from them, as Proverbs 6:6 and 30:24-31 do. Either way his wisdom took in the whole living world.

decisions.choice: from the cedar to the hyssop: from the greatest plant to the least
decisions.reason: The cedar of Lebanon was the tallest and noblest tree people knew; hyssop was a small bushy plant that could grow in cracks of a wall (Exodus 12:22). The pair includes everything between.

decisions.choice: beasts, birds, creeping things and fish: the creatures of Genesis 1
decisions.reason: The four groups are the living creatures over which humankind was given rule (Genesis 1:26; 9:2).

decisions.choice: trees and plants; little hyssop plant; creatures that crawl on the ground (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that hyssop is a small plant (m2) and explains "creeping things".

decisions.choice: "cây bá hương"; "cây kinh giới"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese Bible names for the cedar and the hyssop; the pair runs from the greatest plant to the least (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "백향목" for cedar
decisions.reason: The cedar of Lebanon is 백향목 in Samuel and the Psalms, kept through the temple chapters.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה מֵאֵת֙ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶת־חָכְמָתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they came from all the peoples to hear [the] wisdom of Solomon, from all [the] kings of the earth who had heard his wisdom.

en.L: And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
en.B: People came from all the nations to hear Solomon's wisdom; they came on behalf of all the kings of the earth, who had heard how wise he was.
en.R: People came from every nation to listen to Solomon's wisdom. Kings all over the world had heard how wise he was, and they sent people to hear him.

es.L: Y venían de todos los pueblos a oír la sabiduría de Salomón, de parte de todos los reyes de la tierra que habían oído de su sabiduría.
es.B: De todas las naciones venía gente a escuchar la sabiduría de Salomón; venían de parte de todos los reyes de la tierra, que habían oído lo sabio que era.
es.R: Gente de todas las naciones venía a escuchar la sabiduría de Salomón. Los reyes de todo el mundo habían oído lo sabio que era, y enviaban personas para escucharlo.

fr.L: Et on vint de tous les peuples pour entendre la sagesse de Salomon, de la part de tous les rois de la terre qui avaient entendu parler de sa sagesse.
fr.B: On venait de toutes les nations pour entendre la sagesse de Salomon ; on venait de la part de tous les rois de la terre, qui avaient appris combien il était sage.
fr.R: Des gens sont venus de toutes les nations pour écouter la sagesse de Salomon. Partout dans le monde, des rois avaient entendu dire qu’il était très sage, et ils ont envoyé des gens pour l’écouter.

sw.L: Wakaja kutoka kwa mataifa yote kusikia hekima ya Sulemani, kutoka kwa wafalme wote wa dunia waliokuwa wamesikia habari za hekima yake.
sw.B: Watu walikuja kutoka mataifa yote kusikia hekima ya Sulemani; walikuja kwa niaba ya wafalme wote wa dunia waliokuwa wamesikia jinsi alivyokuwa na hekima.
sw.R: Watu walikuja kutoka kila taifa kusikiliza hekima ya Sulemani. Wafalme wa dunia yote walikuwa wamesikia jinsi alivyokuwa na hekima, nao wakatuma watu kumsikiliza.

vi.L: Người ta từ mọi dân đến để nghe sự khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn, từ tất cả các vua trên đất đã nghe về sự khôn ngoan của vua.
vi.B: Người ta từ mọi dân tộc đến nghe sự khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn; họ được sai đến từ tất cả các vua trên đất đã nghe vua khôn ngoan thế nào.
vi.R: Người ta từ mọi nước đến nghe sự khôn ngoan của Sa-lô-môn. Các vua trên khắp thế giới đã nghe vua khôn ngoan thế nào, nên họ sai người đến nghe vua.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 모든 백성 가운데서, 그의 지혜를 들은 세상의 모든 왕에게서 솔로몬의 지혜를 들으러 왔다.
ko.B: 모든 민족에게서 사람들이 솔로몬의 지혜를 들으러 왔다. 그들은 솔로몬이 지혜롭다는 소문을 들은 세상 모든 왕이 보낸 사람들이었다.
ko.R: 모든 나라에서 사람들이 솔로몬의 지혜로운 말을 들으러 왔다. 세상의 모든 왕이 그가 얼마나 지혜로운지 소문을 듣고 사람들을 보내 그의 말을 듣게 했다.

decisions.choice: from all the kings of the earth: sent by kings
decisions.reason: "From the kings" most likely means that people came on behalf of kings, as their envoys. Some kings came themselves, as the queen of Sheba did (10:1-13).

decisions.choice: the world comes to hear Solomon's wisdom
decisions.reason: This is told at length in 10:1-13 and again in 10:23-24.

decisions.choice: they sent people to hear him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says how people came "from" the kings (m1).

source.text: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צ֤וֹר אֶת־עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י אֹת֛וֹ מָשְׁח֥וּ לְמֶ֖לֶךְ תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑יהוּ כִּ֣י אֹהֵ֗ב הָיָ֥ה חִירָ֛ם לְדָוִ֖ד כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And sent Hiram king of Tyre his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that him they had anointed [as] king in place of his father; for a friend had been Hiram to David all the days.

en.L: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had been a friend to David all the days.
en.B: Hiram king of Tyre sent his officials to Solomon when he heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father's place, for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
en.R: Hiram, the king of Tyre, had always been a friend of David. So when he heard that Solomon had been anointed king to take his father's place, he sent his officials to Solomon.

es.L: Y envió Hiram, rey de Tiro, a sus siervos a Salomón, porque oyó que lo habían ungido rey en lugar de su padre; porque Hiram había sido siempre amigo de David.
es.B: Hiram, rey de Tiro, envió a sus oficiales a Salomón al saber que había sido ungido rey en lugar de su padre, porque Hiram siempre había sido amigo de David.
es.R: Hiram, el rey de Tiro, siempre había sido amigo de David. Así que, cuando oyó que Salomón había sido ungido rey para ocupar el lugar de su padre, envió a sus oficiales a ver a Salomón.

fr.L: Et Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya ses serviteurs vers Salomon, car il avait appris qu’on l’avait oint comme roi à la place de son père ; car Hiram avait été ami de David tous les jours.
fr.B: Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya ses officiers auprès de Salomon quand il apprit qu’on l’avait oint comme roi à la place de son père, car Hiram avait toujours été un ami de David.
fr.R: Hiram, le roi de Tyr, avait toujours été un ami de David. Alors quand il a appris que Salomon avait reçu l’onction pour devenir roi à la place de son père, il a envoyé ses officiers auprès de Salomon.

sw.L: Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro akatuma watumishi wake kwa Sulemani, kwa maana alikuwa amesikia kwamba wamempaka mafuta [awe] mfalme mahali pa baba yake; kwa maana Hiramu alikuwa rafiki wa Daudi siku zote.
sw.B: Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro aliwatuma maafisa wake kwa Sulemani aliposikia kwamba Sulemani amepakwa mafuta kuwa mfalme mahali pa baba yake, kwa kuwa Hiramu alikuwa rafiki wa Daudi siku zote.
sw.R: Hiramu, mfalme wa Tiro, alikuwa rafiki wa Daudi siku zote. Basi aliposikia kwamba Sulemani amepakwa mafuta kuwa mfalme mahali pa baba yake, akawatuma maafisa wake kwa Sulemani.

vi.L: Hi-ram vua Ty-rơ sai các đầy tớ mình đến với Sa-lô-môn, vì ông nghe rằng người ta đã xức dầu cho Sa-lô-môn làm vua thay cha mình; vì Hi-ram luôn là bạn của Đa-vít.
vi.B: Hi-ram vua Ty-rơ sai các quần thần đến với Sa-lô-môn khi nghe tin Sa-lô-môn đã được xức dầu làm vua thay cha mình, vì Hi-ram vốn luôn là bạn của Đa-vít.
vi.R: Hi-ram, vua Ty-rơ, vốn luôn là bạn của Đa-vít. Vì vậy, khi nghe tin Sa-lô-môn được xức dầu làm vua thay cha mình, ông sai các quan chức đến gặp Sa-lô-môn.

ko.L: 그리고 두로 왕 히람이 자기 신하들을 솔로몬에게 보냈다. 사람들이 그에게 기름을 부어 그의 아버지를 대신하여 왕으로 세웠다는 소식을 들었기 때문이다. 히람은 언제나 다윗의 벗이었다.
ko.B: 두로 왕 히람은 솔로몬이 기름 부음을 받고 아버지의 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다는 소식을 듣고, 자기 신하들을 솔로몬에게 보냈다. 히람은 늘 다윗과 친하게 지냈기 때문이다.
ko.R: 두로 왕 히람은 늘 다윗과 친하게 지냈다. 그래서 솔로몬이 기름 부음을 받고 아버지를 이어 왕이 되었다는 소식을 듣고, 자기 신하들을 솔로몬에게 보냈다.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: this verse is 5:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Hebrew 5:1-14 is numbered 4:21-34 in many Bibles, so the account of Hiram and the building materials (5:15-32 here) is numbered 5:1-18 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: Hiram king of Tyre: ruler of the great Phoenician port
decisions.reason: Tyre was a trading city on the coast north of Israel, built partly on an island. Hiram had sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's house (2 Samuel 5:11).

decisions.choice: a friend: an ally bound by a treaty
decisions.reason: The word means "one who loves". Between kings it is the language of alliance: a king who "loves" another is his faithful treaty partner. Hiram's friendship with David now passes to David's son.

decisions.choice: they had anointed him: he had been anointed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they anointed" without naming who; the sense is that Solomon had been made king (1:39).

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These are a king's envoys, so Balanced and Readable call them officials, as these books do for a king's servants.

decisions.choice: "Hiram, rey de Tiro"
decisions.reason: Hiram of Tyre follows the Kings terms note, the same form as in 2 Samuel 5:11. Spanish says "amigo" at every level for the ally of a treaty, as the English does.

vi.B: Sa-lô-môn sai người đến nói với Hi-ram:
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn sai người mang lời nhắn này đến cho Hi-ram:
